text: The lab results show an elevated white blood cell count, which is concerning for infection, while your metabolic panel and toxicology screen are normal. Have you noticed any stiff neck, sensitivity to light, or a new rash while you have been feverish?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information; the elevated WBC confirms an infection. Given your history of tics and current use of haloperidol, have you noticed any muscle stiffness, painful spasms, or difficulty swallowing since starting or increasing this medication? Also, do you have any history of kidney disease or are you currently taking a thiazide diuretic?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fever and altered mentation. I also have Profuse sweating, Generalized rigidity, Confusion and disorientation, Ability to move all limbs, Normal deep tendon reflexes with bilateral downgoing plantar responses.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome.

The clinical picture of fever, altered mental status, generalized rigidity, and profuse sweating in a patient taking haloperidol is classic for NMS. The normal deep tendon reflexes help distinguish this from serotonin syndrome or tetanus.
